purpose: Decide whether market theses expressed in different vocabulary cluster together under embedding similarity. This is the load-bearing assumption of the mind knowledge-base design (docs/2026-08-06-consensus-and-source-weighting.md): if paraphrases of one thesis do not outrank lexically-similar decoys, the thesis axis is noise and the design falls back to ticker and creator.
author: memo
for: embeddings — to run against whatever is currently served (qwen3-embedding-4b @2560 as of today)
how_to_score: Embed every `a` and `b` and every decoy independently, as DOCUMENTS (not queries) unless testing the asymmetry separately.
For each pair: rank all other texts in the file by cosine similarity to `a`. Record the rank of its true partner `b`.
PRIMARY METRIC: recall@1 — fraction of pairs where `b` is the nearest neighbour of `a` among all candidates.
SECONDARY: mean reciprocal rank, and recall@5.
REPORT ALSO: for each pair, whether any decoy outranked the true partner, and which. That is the diagnostic, not the score.
Run a->b and b->a separately. Asymmetric results are themselves a finding.
why_the_decoys_matter: The easy version of this test is trivially passed and proves nothing. Every decoy here is designed to SHARE VOCABULARY with a pair while meaning something different, or to mean something adjacent while sharing no vocabulary. If the model ranks by surface overlap it will fail specifically on these, and that failure is the whole point of running it.

interpretation.recall@1 >= 0.8: thesis axis is real; proceed with clustering as designed
interpretation.recall@1 0.5-0.8: usable only with LLM canonicalization at ingest first, then re-test on the canonical forms
interpretation.recall@1 < 0.5: thesis clustering by embedding does not work on this text; fall back to ticker + creator axes, or make canonicalization mandatory and re-test
interpretation.caveat: These are hand-written by an LLM, not drawn from mind's real corpus. A pass here is necessary, not sufficient — real transcript claims are longer, messier, and hedged. Treat a pass as permission to test on 50 real claim pairs from mind, not as the answer.

note_on_the_hard_cases: Decoys d15, d19, d22, d25, d28, d29, d30 are single-word or single-phrase edits that REVERSE meaning while preserving nearly all vocabulary. If the model cannot separate these from true paraphrases, then embedding similarity is measuring topic rather than claim — which for a thesis store is the difference between 'these people are talking about the same subject' and 'these people are making the same argument'. The design needs the second. Report performance on this subset separately; it is more informative than the headline number.
